crime_highlights: When accosted by the asset protection officer, Mr. Fernandez resisted and struck him with a syringe
The syringe was imbedded in the officer's hand
the assault with the needle has caused him physical symptoms, along with the anxiety and distress of not knowing whether he had been infected
rationale_highlights: The mitigating circumstances are set out in the report provided by B.C. Mental Health and Substance Use Services
Mr. Fernandez has had a difficult upbringing
He is a First Nations man who has waived any requirements for a Gladue report, namely as a result of those factors being addressed in the report from Mental Health
He was adopted at 16 months of age, but ended up spending time in a number of foster care homes where he was physically and sexually abused
note: Background listed as mitigating; Gladue waived; no stated effect of systemic factor

crime_highlights: On September 9, 2012, she was brutally beaten, likely with a dowel, about the head and body
She lay bleeding from her wounds in an abandoned house
She was left to die alone in these circumstances after Mr. Johnny left the scene
Regrettably, she succumbed, and she was pronounced dead in the early morning hours on September 10, 2012
Mr. Johnny did not leave to seek immediate help for her
rationale_highlights: Mr. Johnny's mother is a survivor of the St. Michael's Indian Residential School, and she was a witness to and target of abuse
As a consequence of his parents' struggle with alcohol and substance abuse, he left the reserve at age 15
I am mindful of his background, as I have set out in detail in reference to the Gladue report, and of his family and present situations
note: Court only says it is mindful of Gladue background; no stated effect

crime_highlights: when she started to scream, the accused put his hand over her mouth and told her to shut up
he told her that if she ever told her aunty, he would hurt her
rationale_highlights: all available sanctions, other than imprisonment, that are reasonable in the circumstances and consistent with the harm done to victims or to the community should be considered for all offenders, with particular attention to the circumstances of Aboriginal offenders
Crown has identified, in their view, the only mitigating factor which is the aboriginal heritage of E.J.T.M.
note: Only Crown names heritage as mitigating; joint submission; court states no effect
